paragraphs.en: You normally start with five dice and can see only your own roll. Press V to read it. A bid covers everyone’s dice: three fours, for example, means there are at least three dice showing four across the table.

Press B to choose a quantity and a face, or use the arrows and Enter to select the lowest legal bid for a face. L repeats the current bid. Raise by bidding more dice or by keeping the quantity and naming a higher face.
Press K to challenge the last bid. Everyone reveals their dice. If the bid was too high, the bidder loses a die. If there are at least as many as claimed, you lose a die instead.

In the default variant, D calls the exact count. If you are right, everyone else loses a die and you open the next round. If you are wrong, you lose a die. After a bluff challenge, the player who lost a die starts, or the next player if they are out. When you lose your last die you are out. The last player with dice wins.
Classic has no exact calls, and ones count as themselves.

In Perudo, ones count as wild for other faces. You cannot open an ordinary round with ones. To switch to ones, bid at least half the previous quantity rounded up. To switch back, bid at least twice the number of ones plus one. To raise a bid of ones without changing face, bid more ones.

With Palifico enabled, a player’s first loss down to one die changes the next round if at least three players remain. Ones are not wild. Only players who have opened a Palifico round can change the face of a bid.

With Calza enabled, press D to call the exact quantity, even out of turn, unless it is your own bid. A correct call gets one die back, up to the starting limit; the last player to lose a die then opens. A wrong call costs you a die.
If disconnected, return with the same ELTEN profile to keep access to your dice. While dice are hidden, you cannot save the game or transfer those dice to someone else.
D: call the exact count when allowed
